messages:
maria: heads up — fw 1.4.2 rollout to BMCs in ap-south1 started ~16:45 UTC. seeing large NTP slew events on OOB jump hosts and a bunch of provisioning timeouts. paging eng-oncall :eyes:
jason: logs? any console snippets?
maria: small snippet from jump1 right when reprovision started:
```
Jun 18 16:46:12 jump1 chronyd[1234]: System clock slew 238ms (rate 520ppm)
Jun 18 16:46:15 provisioner: serial-console timeout waiting for tty (300s)
Jun 18 16:47:01 bmc-fw: pushed time update to host before console ready
```
liam: is this chronyd doing a slew instead of stepping? could be because RTC jumped and chrony is configured to slew only.
tara: we saw a variant of this on 1.3.8 where BMC pushed time early and secure-boot checks failed because machine identity rotated during the window. worth checking keystore write ordering.
maria: correct — hypothesis: BMC pushes NTP/time before the host's provisioning agent finishes SSH/console handshake. the large slew causes the agent's cert checks to fail intermittently, provisioner retries, nodes stay in queue.
jason: what's the hit? how many nodes/racks? cost impact?
maria: current snapshot: 34 nodes stuck in provisioning queue across 6 racks (~272 GPUs affected). If we keep rolling at this rate we'll need to spin up fallback burst capacity — rough estimate +$2.3k/hr while backlog clears.
liam: mitigation suggestions: 1) pause rollout and rollback canary racks to 1.4.1; 2) add an fw precheck to delay NTP push until console/ssh is healthy; 3) set a conservative chrony maxslew on jump hosts during rollouts.
tara: agree on pause. also add secure-boot postflash healthcheck to run after keystore rotation. keystore rotation is slow (3-5m/rack) so factor into timing.
deploy-bot: canary-check: 3 nodes tested — 1 succeeded, 2 failed. auto-pause engaged by deploy policy.
maria: pausing rollout for the remaining 42 racks now. opening incident INC-4122 and paging eng-oncall. will run targeted rollback on the two failing canary racks next. :fire_engine:
jason: I'll open a quick PR to add ntp-slew limit to the fw precheck and a unit test for the provisioner race — PR #842.
liam: also tagging infra-test to add a repro that applies NTP push before console ready — want deterministic CI coverage.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-4122 | severity: P2 | owner: eng-oncall | link: https://incidents/internal/INC-4122
tara: runbook reminder: follow runbook section 4 for rollback (keystore rotation caveat). ETA for rollback + re-provisioning for the two canaries ~45-60m.
maria: thanks — I'll collate logs and follow up with a short post-incident writeup once we've confirmed root cause. in the meantime hold any other fw pushes to out-of-band until runbook change lands. :thumbsup:
